title: Arsenal 1-1 Borussia Dortmund: Gyokeres' early screamer not enough
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutArsenal 1-1 Borussia Dortmund: Gyokeres' early screamer not enoughShareViktor Gyokeres scored a stunner to put Arsenal ahead against Borussia Dortmund, but then missed a golden chance to snatch all three points.Bundesliga leaders Borussia Dortmund made Arsenal pay for their profligacy as they fought back to draw 1-1 in an enthralling Champions League clash.
Viktor Gyokeres' thunderbolt put Arsenal ahead at Emirates Stadium, but Maximilian Beier's second-half finish ensured a share of the spoils for Dortmund.
A dominant start from Arsenal might have seen the Gunners go ahead inside the opening few minutes, but Christos Tzolis failed to keep his cool after meeting Noni Madueke's centre.
But Arsenal's opener arrived in the 10th minute, with Gyokeres sending a thunderous strike dipping in over Gregor Kobel, who was making his 50th Champions League appearance.
The Gunners could easily have added to their lead. Tzolis was denied by Kobel, with Madueke blazing over on the rebound, while a last-ditch Nico Schlotterbeck challenge frustrated Declan Rice.

Dortmund did offer a scare towards the end of the first half, though, when Arsenal's stand-in goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga had to ensure he got across to stem a chance, and Niko Kovac's team went even closer shortly after the restart when Beier failed to nudge in from Daniel Svensson's centre.
There was also a very good shout for a Dortmund penalty, when a whipped-in cross clearly hit Gyokeres' arm, but the officials let Arsenal off the hook.
Beier did not pass up his next opportunity. After a fantastic run from Joane Gadou, Dortmund's forward set himself on his stronger left foot and planted a fine finish into the bottom-right corner.

Piero Hincapie headed at Kobel as Arsenal sought a swift response, but BVB thought they had gone 2-1 up when Jobe Bellingham tucked home on the rebound, only for the offside flag to cut the visitors' celebrations short.
Gyokeres should have restored Arsenal's lead in the 75th minute, but having met Martin Odegaard's sublime cross, he sent his close-range header well off target.
A goalmouth scramble then saw Serhou Guirassy deflect against Kobel's left-hand post, before Rice struck the woodwork as BVB held on.
Mikel Arteta's team finished with 30 shots and 2.34 expected goals (xG) to their name, but they lacked the clinical edge that has seen them edge out so many tight games over the past year or so.
Dortmund only had 13 attempts, worth a combined 0.92 xG, but they matched the Gunners for shots on target (four) and big chances (four).

Arteta will look back on the first half, in particular, with plenty of frustration. His playmakers were in fine form, as Odegaard and Madueke both created 4+ chances. It is the first time two Arsenal players have done that in the opening half of a Champions League game on record (since 2003-04).
Arsenal's 14 shots, meanwhile, were the most Dortmund have faced on record in the first half of a Champions League game.

But it was only Gyokeres' stunner that separated the sides at the break. The Sweden international has scored in back-to-back Champions League starts for just the second time, after also doing so for Sporting CP in October/November 2024.
Ultimately, though, Gyokeres squandered that huge chance to put Arsenal back in front. He finished the game having had seven shots, but only landed two of those on target.

However, the Gunners nevertheless became just the third English team to go 20+ games unbeaten (W14 D6) in the European Cup/Champions League (excluding penalty shoot-outs), after Manchester United (25 – September 2007-May 2009) and Manchester City (26 – September 2022-October 2024).
